_comment_record_hz: Section H's mandatory high-risk list: "Mandatory for the highest-risk segments: S01+S02 (opening), S04 (tournament), X02 (build), X01 (controller/menu stress), CB-06 + CB-07 + Warden (representative combat), every band handoff +/-60 s (region transitions), X05 (save/load), S10 (finale)." This segment is on that list, so its baseline is 0.5 Hz rather than the 0.1 Hz journey default. Set by the Gate F coordinator, not a transcription choice. Cost is measured, not assumed: one readback+encode at 1920x1080 is 126.5 ms mean on this container, which at 0.5 Hz amortises to 1.054 ms/frame -- over the ~1 ms/frame line section 3 asks about. Section H requires the density here anyway; the overhead note carries the number so a reader can see what the density cost rather than being told it was free.
title: Controller/menu exhaustion matrix (protocol E.4 / section 8)
_source: docs/acceptance/GATE_F_MASTER_PROTOCOL.md E.4, transcribed mechanically per docs/acceptance/GATE_F_INSTRUMENTATION_REQUEST.md section 6. Entry saves per protocol B: S03-exit (all systems unlocked in village) and S08-exit (riding/late menus).
_lane: SEGMENT_SCHEMA.md lists `journey` and `diag` as the lane values. This segment is neither: protocol 0.1 names two lanes, JOURNEY (S01-S10) and STUDY/DIAG (X01-X08), and only the segments prefixed DIAG- inside that second lane may take a shortcut. `study` is that distinction written down rather than collapsed into `diag`, which would read as permission this segment does not have. The field is informational either way -- the per-step `diag` flag is what actually permits a shortcut, and no step here carries one.
_goal: E.4's own words: 'Goal: input ownership collisions.' The matrix crosses every physical control with every context, each context entered through its production path.
_no_teleport: X01 is not a DIAG segment and contains no teleport step. It branches from real journey saves so the study starts from a real player state (protocol B), and section 0.6 forbids sourcing any pacing, navigation, difficulty or economy claim from a shortcut.
_matrix_shape: 19 physical controls x 22 contexts = 418 probe_cell steps. The 19 are E.4's own list of physical controls; the 22 are E.4's own list of contexts MINUS the starter picker and the naming grid, which E.4 marks '(S02 only -- record there)'.
_restore: probe_cell does not establish or restore its own context (SEGMENT_SCHEMA.md). A cell whose control owns the context boundary -- A, B, Y, View, Start, LB, RB in a menu -- can leave the context it was probing, so those cells are followed by an explicit re-entry through the same production path. Where re-entry is not scriptable (a running fight, an in-progress conversation) the cell is followed by an assert on the context instead, which is E.4's `recoverable` column stated as a verdict.
_comment_evidence_lane: §H/§G evidence split, owner decision 2026-08-27, recorded in docs/acceptance/GATE_F_MASTER_PROTOCOL.md §H.1. This is the LOGIC lane: the journey run headless for mechanics, telemetry and step verdicts at 6.1 ms/frame against 12,721 ms for a rendered frame on the Gate F container. It takes no prescribed frame; the §G ids its steps would have taken are DELEGATED to X01C, which declares each of them in its "owes" list. The harness refuses to start this segment if X01C does not exist, does not declare evidence_lane=capture, or does not accept every id handed to it -- a delegation nobody accepted is a debt that has quietly stopped existing, which is the same shape as the 9,231 file:null PASSes CD-1 was written for. Whether the debt was actually PAID is a question about the whole run directory and is answered by tools/gate_f/run_inventory.py, not here.
_comment_record_hz_split: AMENDED for the §H/§G evidence split. record_hz is forced to 0 on a logic lane by the harness regardless of what this file says, because §H's continuous record is the thing the split removes: the recorder's cadence is counted in PLAY seconds now, but under a 12.7 s rendered frame even a 0.1 Hz record fires on every rendered frame, and the eighteen segments' 4,607,802 physics frames are ~8,283 hours. The obligation is not dropped -- §H's prescribed frames move to X01C, which may run BOUNDED record windows around a named state.

steps.title: the world owns input before this walk
steps.expected: no narrative modal is holding locomotion when this walk starts
steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6 modal-holds-locomotion audit. A walk that begins while a narrative modal still owns input does not fail as 'a modal is open' -- it fails as 'did not reach', many steps and sometimes many minutes later, which is how X04 lost its whole combat block to 3601 held frames. This assert is diagnostic and changes no behaviour: it turns that silent cascade into one named cause at the point of origin. RIG-25's rule, applied to narrative modals rather than to shop panels.

steps.title: VOCABULARY GAP: the keyboard half of a dual-bound action cannot be selected

args.text: operator_harness.gd::_physical_binding prefers a joypad event, then a key, then a mouse button, and SEGMENT_SCHEMA.md's `press` has no `device` argument. So W/A/S/D (move_*), E (interact), I (inventory), M (map), Esc (game_menu/menu_cancel) and Tab (menu_tab_right) are all ALSO bound to the pad and will be injected as pad events, not as keys. Only the keyboard-only and mouse-only actions -- B (build_open), L (torch_toggle), F (combat_throw), Esc-as-combat_run, P (torch_place), LMB (use_tool) -- actually reach the KBM path through this vocabulary. Transcribed as written; the gap is reported before the freeze because a `device` argument is a harness change, not an operator change.

steps.expected: a note event carries this observation into events.jsonl
